description: Cream stone with a warm gold star at its heart, left by Sorrel. It still knows the way to the gate.
lore: Fifty-five gold, which is nothing, and it is on every carrier walking every road between fires. Cream, softly mottled, a gold burst low and off-centre in the heart of it like a lit window seen across a field. What it does is unglamorous and worth more than stones costing five times as much: your feet keep the last hour of a long day as though it were the third, and a full pack stops being an argument you are having with yourself. In a fight it is worth precisely nothing.

Graders say what is at the bottom of it flatly, because it is not a mystery. Not speed. The willingness to do the whole day again tomorrow. [[monsters/chestnut_horse|Sorrel]] is remembered for standing at a gate at dusk waiting to be brought in, and the standing is what people walk out to look at — but a stone is a fairer record of a life than the picture anybody carries of it. What went all the way down was not the waiting. It was the coming back up the slope, every evening, for however many years it has been now. [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] wears one and does not pretend it is for the walking: she carries paper and ink out to people who are thinning, she is losing that race by about one person a season, and the stone gets her as far as the next one.
gm_notes: The creature record is about the waiting; the stone is the correction — what pressed down was the returning, not the standing, and only a stone can settle which. Osric's rope and apple and Jehanne's dusk appointment belong to that record and are left there. Bettany's beat is new and is her real want in one line: she is racing the thinning and losing on a measurable schedule. The price is the sting — a working life grades out at fifty-five gold.
